[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Zero Remainder Array** [CF 1374D · Zero Remainder Array](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1374/D){rating="1400"}

Only the residue $r = a_i \bmod k$ matters, exactly as in @sec-gcd-p4-balance - but here an
element with residue $r > 0$ is fixed by *any* $x \equiv (k - r) \pmod k$, and $x$ only ever
increases by one per move. So all elements that want the same residue class $d = k - r$ are
served at $x = d,\, d + k,\, d + 2k, \ldots$ - a family of $\mathit{cnt}[d]$ elements costs
its last member $(\mathit{cnt}[d] - 1)\cdot k + d$ moves. The answer is the largest such
value over all classes, **plus one** because after the final element is served `x` still
increments. This is the residue histogram of @sec-gcd-a3 pushed to its counting conclusion.

[Solved in full in @sec-gcd-p4-zeromod.]{.card-link}

:::
